note:
**Derby House on the 1939 Register - the Wilkinsons still keeping it, twenty-eight years after the 1911 census.** Schedule 1, nine people, transcribed by A. Hagues.

**The house passed from mother to daughter.** Sarah kept it in 1911; here the proprietress is **Mabell M Wilkinson**, born 25 August 1876 - the "Maybell" of 24 on the 1901 Beechwood page - and her sister **Florence**, born 4 June 1874, is retired in the same house. Three censuses and a register hold the same family: Beechwood in 1901, Derby House in 1911 and 1939.

**Florence's birth date settles a discrepancy.** The 1901 page implies 1875 and the 1911 page 1881; the register gives 4 June 1874 outright, which is why she is bound by number in all three rather than created again.

**Gertrude Mary Elizabeth Dainty (#1144) was already in the record** from the 1921 census, and is here as a companion help of 64.

**The register is shaped unlike a census.** It has no relationship column at all, so none is supplied; the household is held together by its schedule number, and the sub numbers 1 to 9 give the order of the nine on the page, recorded in each source line. The birth dates are exact, which a census never gives.

**Five of the nine are new to the record** - the solicitors William Moss and Herbert Hutchinson, Eric Walter Price a chartered accountant, and two manservants, William Alfred Bird and Frank John H Bletcher, the latter seventeen years old. Boarders of a professional kind, which is what the house had taken in since at least 1911.
source: 1939 Register, schedule 1, Derby House, 1 Derby Terrace, Nottingham, transcribed by A. Hagues.
